items.title: Jerry Dodgion interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: I remember this so well because in order to get the band and Joe together the scheduling was ridiculous... Joe Williams, during that week was working at the Half Note... then he would make this, start coming in for one of these records at seven o'clock.

ctx.x: Remember that one? I think you played on that one too.

Oh, with Joe Williams. Oh, now he’s another special case. Oh, man. We met when I was with Red Norvo we played Las Vegas a lot, and when the band started coming to the Flamingo there, they’d come in for three or four weeks at a time sometimes. And so we met Joe, and he’s a really beautiful person, and he was part of the band. He was not a star with the band. I mean they traveled together these guys, and they roomed together, and he was just like one of the guys in the band. You know, there was a humanity thing…
I guess they just meant that the band didn’t tour around the country. I mean gee a gig at the Vanguard is hardly a rehearsal.
